notes:
CIRCUIT: a two-source ladder. An AC current source I-AC #6 (33 sin t A) and a 4 kohm Resistor #7 sit in parallel on the left between a top rail (y~432) and a bottom rail (y~656). From that node the top rail runs right through R 5 kohm #0, L 20 mH #1 to a mid node at x~594, where C 4 nF #4 drops to the bottom rail / GND #8, then on through L 5 mH #2 and R 2 kohm #3 to the AC voltage source V-AC #5 (30 sin t V) on the right, whose bottom returns along the bottom rail. 9 components, 6 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1 = left top node: top lead of I-AC #6 (159,512), top lead of R4k #7 (320,515) via the T at S20 (314,432), and the left lead of R5k #0 (397,431) - all on the top rail y~432 from x~160 to x~397.
  n2 = short link between the right end of R5k #0 (~x488, y428) and the left end of L20mH #1 (~x496, y428). Solid ink, verified by inkmap at (491,431): an unbroken horizontal stroke at y=428-429 running from the resistor's last diagonal (x~476) into the inductor's first coil (x~509).
  n3 = right lead of L20mH #1 (577,434) -> top rail east to the T at S21 (594,435) -> down to the top plate of C4nF #4 (596,499); the rail also continues east to the left lead of L5mH #2 (651,434).
  n4 = link between the right end of L5mH #2 (~x735, y438) and the left end of R2k #3 (~x756, y438). Solid ink, verified by inkmap at (742,437): a continuous horizontal stroke at y=438-439 joining the inductor's last coil to the resistor's first upstroke.
  n5 = right lead of R2k #3 (836,432) -> top rail east to x~877 -> down to the top lead of V-AC #5 (877,503).
  0  = bottom rail y~656: bottom lead of I-AC #6 (162,588) -> rail -> T at S37 (322,656) to the bottom lead of R4k #7 (321,608) -> rail east -> node at S36 (604,653) where the bottom lead of C4nF #4 (602,550) comes down and continues on down to GND #8 (608,655) -> rail east -> bottom lead of V-AC #5 (880,569).

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all four, each verified in the raw pixels):
  S20 (314,432) - JUNCTION. inkmap: the top rail is solid across y=431-433 and a vertical stub begins at y=434 (x=312-315) heading down; there is no ink above the rail. Clean T, so junction. The other reading is not even available for a T; treating it as 'none' would strand R4k's top terminal on a one-terminal net and remove the 4 kohm branch from the circuit.
  S21 (594,435) - JUNCTION. inkmap: top rail solid across y=433-435, vertical stub begins at y=436 (x=592-597) heading down to the capacitor; nothing above the rail. Clean T. Reading it as a crossing would leave the capacitor's top plate on a one-terminal net and delete the shunt branch that defines the ladder.
  S36 (604,653) - JUNCTION. This is the busiest node: the capacitor's vertical drop arrives from above at x=601-602, the bottom rail runs solid across y=652-653, and the ink continues below the rail (x=602-607, thickened to ~6 px for y=654-659) down to the GND top bar at y=673. The tracer flagged hop=2.1, but the pixels show no semicircular hop and no sideways jog - the vertical runs straight through and is in fact fattened at the crossing (dot=2.0), which is the drafter's solder blob. Junction. The crossing reading would split the sheet into a floating bottom rail (I-AC, R4k and V-AC bottoms with no ground reference) plus a dead-end capacitor+GND pair carrying no current - electrically impossible for this circuit, so rule 1 settles it even without the blob.
  S37 (322,656) - JUNCTION. inkmap: bottom rail solid across y=655-657 with a vertical stub arriving from above at x=322-324 and terminating on it (only a 2-row pen overshoot below). Clean T. Same argument as S20: the other reading would strand R4k's bottom terminal.

NON-CRITICAL SITES (all recorded as 'junction' = the default, to document that each was opened and looked at): S2, S3, S4, S7, S8, S10, S12, S13, S14, S16, S19 all lie inside the handwritten value labels '5K ohm', '20mH', '5mH' and '2K ohm' sitting just above the top rail; S23, S24, S25 lie inside '30 sin t V'; S32 inside '33 sin t A'; S33 inside '4 K ohm'. None of them involves a wire, and after the port/merge fixes below none of them carries a terminal, so their reading has no effect on the netlist.

PORT FIX:
  #3 Resistor (2 kohm) terminal 1: moved from p2@(814,415) to p4@(836,432). p2 sits on a stroke of the '2K ohm' label (wire_len 7); p4 is the real right lead, wire_len 107 - the same wire the V-AC top port (877,503) sits on. Before the fix R2k.t1 was alone on n7 and V-AC.t0 alone on n8; they now correctly share n5. Terminal 0 of #3 is left on p1@(775,419) - see merge below.
  Unused-port warnings checked and dismissed as label ink rather than leads: #1 p1@(575,409); #2 p1@(657,414) and p2@(697,413); #5 p1@(905,538) and p2@(907,548) (strokes of '30 sin t V'). Ports that were already correct and left alone: #0 p0 (left lead), #1 p0 (right lead), #2 p0 (left lead), #4 p1/p0 (top/bottom plates), #5 p3/p0 (top/bottom), #6 p0/p1 (top/bottom), #7 p0/p1 (top/bottom), #8 p0.

MERGES (why they were necessary): the drafter placed the component bounding boxes almost edge to edge, so the two inter-component link wires are only ~8-12 px long and were swallowed when the tracer deleted the component boxes; consequently no port candidate exists on either lead and 'ports' cannot reach them. In both cases the terminal had instead landed on a stroke of the value label written just above, producing a one-terminal net. I verified the real ink with inkmap before merging.
  merge ['0.1','1.0'] = net n2. R5k #0 terminal 1 was on p1@(414,412), the 'K' of '5K ohm'; L20mH #1 terminal 0 was on p2@(516,410), the '0' of '20mH'. The real link is the unbroken stroke at y=428-429 between x=476 and x=509 (inkmap at 491,431); the wire tracer does see a fragment of it (edge e36, (488,428)-(496,429)) but bound it to neither component. Nothing else is on either net, so the merge produces exactly the 2-terminal net n2 and cannot pull in anything spurious.
  merge ['2.1','3.0'] = net n4. L5mH #2 terminal 1 was on p3@(720,418), the 'H' of '5mH'; R2k #3 terminal 0 was on p1@(775,419), a stroke of '2K ohm'. The real link is the unbroken stroke at y=438-439 between x~735 and x~756 (inkmap at 742,437), also visible in the S14 crop. Here the stub is entirely inside the two dilated boxes so not even a fragment survived in the wire graph. Again both source nets were single-terminal, so the merge yields exactly the 2-terminal net n4.

CLASSES: all nine agree with the drawing - circle with a straight arrow through it and a sine squiggle = I-AC (#6, '33 sin t A'); circle with a sine wave only = V-AC (#5, '30 sin t V'); three zigzags = Resistors (#0 5K, #3 2K, #7 4K); two coil runs = Inductors (#1 20mH, #2 5mH); two parallel plates = Capacitor (#4 4nF); stacked bars = GND (#8). No re-classification proposed. All parts are 2-terminal (plus the 1-terminal GND) so no pin-order question arises.

GAP BRIDGES: 26 reported, none changes the netlist; none dropped.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. There is no plain-X wire crossing anywhere on this sheet - every wire-to-wire meeting is a T or the deliberately blobbed 4-way at S36 - and no lead is drawn going nowhere.
